diagnostics.message: :output.custom_role_id: explicit depends_on of :resource.google_organization_iam_custom_role.roles is redundant — already implied by attribute references

output.custom_role_id lists `depends_on = [google_organization_iam_custom_role.roles]`, but its value is built with `for role_id, role in google_organization_iam_custom_role.roles : ...`, so Terraform already infers that dependency. The explicit depends_on is redundant and can be removed.

google_organization_iam_binding.authoritative binds roles that may be custom roles created in this same module (var.iam/group_iam can reference organizations/<id>/roles/<name>). Binding a just-created custom role fails until the role exists and propagates, and no attribute reference or depends_on expresses this ordering. It should depend on google_organization_iam_custom_role.roles (the same guard every other org-level resource here already uses).

google_organization_iam_member.additive grants roles (var.iam_additive / iam_additive_members) that may be custom roles created in this module. Because the role is supplied as a variable string, Terraform infers no ordering, so the member can be created before the custom role exists/propagates and fail. It should depend on google_organization_iam_custom_role.roles, matching the guard used by the other org-level resources.

google_organization_iam_policy.authoritative sets the whole org IAM policy from data.google_iam_policy.authoritative, whose bindings (var.iam_bindings_authoritative) may reference custom roles created in this module. With no ordering expressed, the authoritative policy can be applied before the custom roles exist/propagate, dropping or failing on those bindings. It should depend on google_organization_iam_custom_role.roles, like the other org-level resources.
